single_prompt_mode.description: Describe your business and ideal customers in your own words. A complete answer includes: what you sell, who buys it (industry, size, geography), who doesn't buy it, example customers, and who you sell to (titles).
single_prompt_mode.placeholder: Tell us everything about your ideal customer...

example.title: Example of a great answer:
example.content:
**BoxFlow** (boxflow.io) sells warehouse management software to mid-size e-commerce companies in the US. Deals range $30K-$150K/year.

**Ideal customer:** $5M-$100M revenue, 50-500 employees, ships 1000+ orders/day, currently using spreadsheets or outdated WMS. Recently raised funding or opened new warehouse = strong buying signal.

**Sell to:** VP/Director of Operations, Logistics, or Supply Chain. Sometimes COO at smaller companies.

**Don't sell to:** 3PLs (competitors' customers), companies already on SAP/Oracle, companies under $3M revenue, outside US.

**Current customers:** acme-shipping.com, fastfulfill.io, boxbrand.com

**Search terms by category:**
- Industry: e-commerce, DTC brand, online retail, Shopify seller
- Problem: fulfillment challenges, warehouse inefficiency, inventory management
- Stage: Series A, growing, scaling, hiring warehouse staff
- Tech: WMS, 3PL alternative, ShipStation, fulfillment software

fields.label: Website URL
fields.subtext: We'll scrape this for additional context

fields.label: What do you sell?
fields.placeholder: Describe your product or service in 1-2 sentences
fields.subtext: e.g., "B2B SaaS for inventory management", "Executive recruiting for tech companies", "Industrial equipment maintenance services"

fields.label: Describe your ideal customer
fields.placeholder: Who is the perfect fit for what you sell?
fields.subtext: e.g., "Mid-size e-commerce companies struggling with warehouse efficiency" or "Series A+ startups needing to scale their engineering team"

fields.label: Target company size
fields.subtext: e.g., employee count (50-500), revenue ($5M-$100M), funding stage (Series A+), or "Fortune 500 only"

fields.label: Geographic requirements
fields.placeholder: Where must your customers be located?
fields.subtext: e.g., "US only", "English-speaking countries", "Must have EU operations", "No restrictions"

fields.label: Seniority levels that can buy
fields.placeholder: What title levels make purchasing decisions?
fields.subtext: e.g., CEO, VP, Director, Manager, Head of, C-Suite, Senior

fields.label: Departments you sell to
fields.subtext: e.g., IT, Marketing, Operations, Finance, HR, Engineering, Sales, Procurement, Legal

fields.label: Who should we exclude?
fields.placeholder: Industries, company types, competitors, or other exclusions
fields.subtext: e.g., "Agencies", "Government", "Companies under $1M revenue", "Competitors: Acme Corp, Beta Inc"

fields.label: Example customers (URLs)
fields.placeholder: Paste 3-10 URLs of ideal customers, separated by commas or new lines
fields.subtext: Current customers, past customers, or companies you wish were customers

fields.label: Search terms that work
fields.subtext: Group by type: Industry terms, Problem terms, Stage/size terms, Technology terms. One term from each group combines into searches.

fields.label: Anything else?
fields.placeholder: Buying signals, timing indicators, or other helpful context
fields.subtext: e.g., "Recently raised funding = strong signal", "Hiring for X role = good timing"

fields.label: Extract individual contacts?
fields.subtext: Find names, titles, and emails of people at each company

search_term_guidance.description: Organize keywords into categories. The system picks one term from each non-empty category and combines them into search queries.

categories.name: Industry/Vertical
categories.description: What industry are your customers in?

categories.name: Product/Problem
categories.description: What product do they have or problem do they face?

categories.name: Company Stage/Size
categories.description: What stage or size signals a good fit?

categories.name: Technology/Tools
categories.description: What technology or tools do they use?

categories.name: Activity/Behavior
categories.description: What are they doing that signals buying intent?
